title_en: Reading day: a ḥadīth with its chain
q_en: Where does the chain end, and where do the words begin?
q_ar: أَيْنَ يَنْتَهِي السَّنَدُ، وَأَيْنَ يَبْدَأُ الْمَتْنُ؟
not_yet: Judging the narrators or the strength of a chain: that is the science of ḥadīth, not this course.
Reading a long ḥadīth without help: more texts come later.
Every name in every chain: look names up in a book of narrators.
not_yet_ar: الْحُكْمُ عَلَى الرُّوَاةِ أَوْ عَلَى قُوَّةِ السَّنَدِ: هَذَا عِلْمُ الْحَدِيثِ، لَيْسَ مَوْضُوعَ هَذَا الدَّرْسِ.
قِرَاءَةُ حَدِيثٍ طَوِيلٍ بِلَا مُسَاعَدَةٍ: نُصُوصٌ أُخْرَى تَأْتِي فِي دُرُوسٍ لَاحِقَةٍ.
كُلُّ اسْمٍ فِي كُلِّ سَنَدٍ: اُطْلُبِ الْأَسْمَاءَ فِي كِتَابِ الرُّوَاةِ.

slides.head_en: Reading day: a ḥadīth with its chain
slides.big_en: Find where the chain ends. Then read the words.
slides.big_ar: أَيْنَ يَنْتَهِي السَّنَدُ؟ وَأَيْنَ يَبْدَأُ الْمَتْنُ؟
slides.small: No new grammar today. You know the words; now learn to see the shape of a ḥadīth.
slides.small_ar: لَا قَاعِدَةَ جَدِيدَةَ الْيَوْمَ. تَعْرِفُ الْكَلِمَاتِ؛ تَعَلَّمِ الْآنَ أَنْ تَرَى شَكْلَ الْحَدِيثِ.

slides.head_en: Look: a short chain, then the words
sents: حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ قَالَ: ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
Ahmad told us, from Ali, who said: The boy went to the mosque.
أَخْبَرَنَا سَالِمٌ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: رَجَعَ الْحَاجُّ إِلَى تَرِيمَ.
Salim informed us, from his father, who said: The pilgrim returned to Tarim.
حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ عَنْ يُوسُفَ قَالَ: كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ رِسَالَةً.
Umar told us, from Yusuf, who said: The student wrote a letter.

lines: Which words join one name to the next? Which word begins the chain?
أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَرْبِطُ اسْمًا بِاسْمٍ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَبْدَأُ بِهَا السِّلْسِلَةُ؟
Which word comes just before the words (the matn)?
أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَأْتِي قَبْلَ الْمَتْنِ مُبَاشَرَةً؟
Count the names. Is the last name always the one who spoke?
عُدَّ الْأَسْمَاءَ. هَلِ الِاسْمُ الْأَخِيرُ هُوَ الَّذِي تَكَلَّمَ؟

cards.def_en: the names of the narrators, joined by “told us” and “from”
the last name is the Companion, who says: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said”
what the Prophet ﷺ said: it begins after قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ

slides.head_en: The chain of the first ḥadīth of al-Arbaʿīn
slides.note: Six names, six links. The chain ends with the Companion; then come the words of the Prophet ﷺ.
slides.note_ar: سِتَّةُ أَسْمَاءٍ وَسِتُّ حَلَقَاتٍ. يَنْتَهِي السَّنَدُ بِالصَّحَابِيِّ، ثُمَّ كَلَامُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.

cards.def_en: root ح د ث: the same root as حَدِيث (a report)
the same job as حَدَّثَنَا in a chain

cards.title_en: may Allah be pleased with him
cards.def_en: said after the name of a Companion

slides.head_en: The chain and the words side by side
slides.note: The word قَالَ stands between them.

slides.why: Salim says: “حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكٌ is the ḥadīth.” Wrong! It is only a link in the chain. The words of the Prophet ﷺ begin after قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ.
slides.why_ar: يَقُولُ سَالِمٌ: «حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكٌ هُوَ الْحَدِيثُ». هَذَا خَطَأٌ! هَذِهِ حَلَقَةٌ مِنَ السَّنَدِ فَقَطْ. كَلَامُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ يَبْدَأُ بَعْدَ «قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ».

slides.head_en: Read: the first ḥadīth of al-Arbaʿīn
lines: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ بْنِ قَعْنَبٍ
ʿAbd Allāh b. Maslama b. Qaʿnab told us:
عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ
from Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd, from Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm,
عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ وَقَّاصٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ قَالَ:
from ʿAlqama b. Waqqāṣ, from ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, who said:
قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّةِ وَإِنَّمَا لِامْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Deeds are by intention, and each person has only what he intended.”
slides.source: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 1907 (the same ḥadīth opens al-Arbaʿīn al-Nawawiyya, no. 1, with slightly different wording)

can: I can find where the chain of a ḥadīth ends and where the words begin.
I can read حَدَّثَنَا، أَخْبَرَنَا and عَنْ in a chain and count the narrators.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَجِدَ أَيْنَ يَنْتَهِي سَنَدُ الْحَدِيثِ وَأَيْنَ يَبْدَأُ الْمَتْنُ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ «حَدَّثَنَا» وَ«أَخْبَرَنَا» وَ«عَنْ» فِي السَّنَدِ وَأَعُدَّ الرُّوَاةَ.

items.en: ★ The Arbaʿīn has بِالنِّيَّاتِ and لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ, but this Muslim text has بِالنِّيَّةِ and لِامْرِئٍ. What does that teach you about quoting a ḥadīth?

items.model: Books can give the same ḥadīth with small differences of wording. Always say which book you are quoting from.

lines: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ.
Ahmad sat in the majlis with the students.
وَقَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ حَدِيثًا مِنْ كِتَابٍ كَبِيرٍ.
And the Habib read a ḥadīth from a big book.
سَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً: حَدَّثَنَا، أَخْبَرَنَا، عَنْ، عَنْ.
Ahmad heard many words: “told us”, “informed us”, “from”, “from”.
سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: مَاذَا فِي هَذَا السَّنَدِ؟
Ahmad asked: What is in this chain?
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: فِيهِ اسْمُ كُلِّ رَجُلٍ سَمِعَ الْحَدِيثَ.
The Habib said: In it is the name of every man who heard the ḥadīth.
السَّنَدُ مِنَ الْمُعَلِّمِ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ.
The chain goes from the teacher to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: هَذَا سَنَدٌ، وَهَذَا مَتْنٌ.
So Ahmad wrote in his book: This is a chain, and this is a matn.
ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ الْحَدِيثَ لِأُمِّهِ.
Then he went home and read the ḥadīth to his mother.

lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
